title: LTS perf baseline results (runtime-1.18-lts) — 2025 Q3
content:
Purpose
This sheet captures 2025 Q3 performance baselines for the Runtime LTS line (runtime-1.18-lts) across canonical workloads + GPU SKUs. These numbers are used as:
- “Known good” baselines for LTS perf gating (patch releases must not regress beyond thresholds unless waived)
- Reference expectations for Dedicated sizing and Private deployment validation
- A sanity-check when kernel/scheduler backports land on LTS

What this is / isn’t
- This is NOT a vendor benchmark; it’s our internal gate baseline on Redwood’s controlled runner pool.
- These are steady-state, warmed-up measurements. Cold-start and cache-miss behavior is tracked separately (observability dashboards).

Baseline snapshot
- Runtime branch: runtime-1.18-lts
- Baseline tag used for these runs: 1.18.0-lts-rc2 (internal)
- Notes: kernel autotune defaults are frozen on LTS per PR-23241; experimental batching heuristic is disabled on LTS candidates (see PR-23366).

Methodology (high-level)
Runners
- Bare-metal runners in perf-canary pool, single-tenant job scheduling, no colocation.
- NVIDIA driver pinned per runner image; clocks not manually locked unless noted.

Runtime config (common)
- Continuous batching enabled
- KV cache enabled
- Prefix cache enabled where applicable (explicitly called out)
- Speculative decoding OFF for all baselines (too sensitive to model/dist changes for LTS gates)

Workloads (canonical)
- CHAT-8K/256: interactive chat with 8k prompt, 256 new tokens (latency focused)
- CHAT-2K/512: mid-context, 512 new tokens (balanced)
- GEN-512/1536: short prompt, long generation (throughput + scheduler stability)
- MIXED-PROD: distribution mix (30% 2k/256, 40% 8k/128, 20% 512/1024, 10% 16k/64); meant to catch scheduler pathologies
- EMBED-512: embedding requests with 512 tokens input
- RERANK-32x128: rerank 32 passages @ 128 tokens each

Model set (Q3 standard)
- Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (chat)
- Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (chat + mixed)
- Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (mixed)
- bge-large-en-v1.5 (embeddings)
- bge-reranker-large (rerank)

Metrics definitions
- TTFT p50/p95: time-to-first-token
- Latency p50/p95: end-to-end request latency (includes queueing)
- Throughput: output tokens/sec/GPU for generative workloads; requests/sec/GPU for embed/rerank

Expected variance (what’s “normal”)
- H100/H200: ±1.5% throughput run-to-run; TTFT p95 can move ±3% on mixed workloads.
- A100-80GB: ±2.5% throughput; TTFT p95 ±4%.
- L40S: ±3–5% throughput; TTFT p95 ±6% (more sensitive to host-side contention + clocks).
- If variance exceeds these bands, treat the run as suspect and rerun after checking runner contention, GPU thermals, and kernel autotune warmup.

Known measurement pitfalls (common causes of false regressions)
1) Autotune warmup / kernel cache
   - First run after runner image update or driver reload can shift p95. Always discard first iteration; run 3, keep median.
2) Tokenizer / client overhead leakage
   - If the harness runs tokenization on the critical path (client-side), TTFT inflates. Ensure “server_tokenize=true” in perf-canary harness configs.
3) Clock / thermal throttling
   - L40S in particular can drift if chassis airflow is degraded. Flag runs where GPU power draw or clocks are below expected bands.
4) Prefix cache state
   - Prefix cache ON can dramatically improve TTFT; prefix cache OFF is baseline unless explicitly called out. Ensure cache is cleared between scenarios.
5) Scheduler queueing artifacts
   - If concurrency ramps too fast, queueing can dominate and masquerade as model/runtime regression. Use standard ramp (60s warmup, 120s measure window).
6) Noisy neighbors on host networking/storage
   - Artifact upload jobs and log shipping spikes can affect tail latency. Ensure “perf-canary isolated” label is set on the runner.

====================================================================
SHEET 1 — Generative workloads (tokens/sec per GPU)
All latencies in milliseconds. Throughput is output tokens/sec/GPU.

Columns:
GPU | Model | Workload | Concurrency | Batch cap | Quant | TTFT p50 | TTFT p95 | Latency p50 | Latency p95 | Throughput | Notes

H100-SXM-80GB | Llama-3.1-8B | CHAT-2K/512 | 32 | 32 | FP16 | 95 | 165 | 820 | 1280 | 1780 | Stable; low variance (≤2%).
H100-SXM-80GB | Llama-3.1-8B | CHAT-8K/256 | 32 | 32 | FP16 | 132 | 240 | 610 | 980 | 1560 | Sensitive to host CPU if harness misconfigured.
H100-SXM-80GB | Llama-3.1-8B | GEN-512/1536 | 64 | 64 | FP16 | 88 | 150 | 2460 | 3180 | 1925 | Scheduler steady; tail mostly decode-bound.
H100-SXM-80GB | Llama-3.1-8B | MIXED-PROD | 96 | 64 | FP16 | 110 | 260 | 990 | 2120 | 1710 | Watch for p95 spikes if backpressure changes.

H100-SXM-80GB | Llama-3.1-70B | CHAT-2K/512 | 16 | 16 | FP8 | 160 | 280 | 1420 | 2320 | 720 | FP8 kernel set pinned for LTS.
H100-SXM-80GB | Llama-3.1-70B | CHAT-8K/256 | 16 | 16 | FP8 | 215 | 410 | 980 | 1680 | 640 | TTFT p95 variance up to ~3%.
H100-SXM-80GB | Llama-3.1-70B | GEN-512/1536 | 24 | 24 | FP8 | 150 | 260 | 4980 | 6420 | 790 | Throughput bound; check KV cache fragmentation changes.
H100-SXM-80GB | Llama-3.1-70B | MIXED-PROD | 32 | 24 | FP8 | 190 | 480 | 1980 | 5320 | 710 | MIXED catches scheduler starvation edge cases.

H200-SXM-141GB | Llama-3.1-70B | CHAT-2K/512 | 16 | 16 | FP8 | 155 | 270 | 1360 | 2200 | 760 | Slight uplift vs H100; stable.
H200-SXM-141GB | Llama-3.1-70B | CHAT-8K/256 | 16 | 16 | FP8 | 205 | 395 | 930 | 1580 | 680 | TTFT improvement mostly memory-bound.
H200-SXM-141GB | Llama-3.1-70B | GEN-512/1536 | 24 | 24 | FP8 | 145 | 255 | 4820 | 6280 | 835 | Treat as separate baseline; do not compare to H100.

A100-SXM-80GB | Llama-3.1-8B | CHAT-2K/512 | 24 | 24 | FP16 | 125 | 220 | 1060 | 1650 | 1080 | More tail variance; rerun if p95 > 1750.
A100-SXM-80GB | Llama-3.1-8B | CHAT-8K/256 | 24 | 24 | FP16 | 170 | 320 | 780 | 1280 | 940 | Context heavy; host memory pressure can skew.
A100-SXM-80GB | Llama-3.1-8B | GEN-512/1536 | 48 | 48 | FP16 | 118 | 205 | 3120 | 4050 | 1145 | Throughput stable within ±2.5%.

A100-SXM-80GB | Llama-3.1-70B | CHAT-2K/512 | 8 | 8 | INT8 | 260 | 460 | 2450 | 4020 | 360 | INT8 path used for A100 baseline.
A100-SXM-80GB | Llama-3.1-70B | CHAT-8K/256 | 8 | 8 | INT8 | 340 | 620 | 1700 | 2980 | 315 | p95 sensitive to scheduler queueing.
A100-SXM-80GB | Llama-3.1-70B | MIXED-PROD | 12 | 10 | INT8 | 310 | 780 | 2980 | 7400 | 335 | Known: long-context slice causes p95 spikes if batching changes.

L40S-48GB | Llama-3.1-8B | CHAT-2K/512 | 16 | 16 | FP16 | 165 | 330 | 1400 | 2350 | 690 | Highest run-to-run variance; check clocks.
L40S-48GB | Llama-3.1-8B | CHAT-8K/256 | 16 | 16 | FP16 | 240 | 520 | 1020 | 1880 | 585 | If TTFT p95 > 600, suspect harness contention.
L40S-48GB | Llama-3.1-8B | GEN-512/1536 | 24 | 24 | FP16 | 155 | 310 | 4050 | 5450 | 720 | Long gen tends to be stable once warmed.

Notes (generative)
- These baselines assume the LTS line has experimental batching heuristic disabled. If enabled for any reason, re-baseline MIXED-PROD (throughput can increase but tail can destabilize).
- MIXED-PROD is the primary canary for scheduler starvation regressions (see backport discussion around scheduler starvation edge case).

====================================================================
SHEET 2 — Mixed model set spot-check (stability + routing equivalence)
Goal: ensure kernel + scheduler changes don’t disproportionately affect non-Llama architectures.

GPU | Model | Workload | Concurrency | Quant | TTFT p50 | TTFT p95 | Latency p95 | Throughput | Notes

H100-SXM-80GB | Qwen2.5-72B | MIXED-PROD | 28 | FP8 | 205 | 520 | 5680 | 690 | If p95 > 6100, check scheduler regression tests.
A100-SXM-80GB | Qwen2.5-72B | CHAT-2K/512 | 8 | INT8 | 295 | 540 | 4680 | 320 | Used as “non-Llama” sanity.

====================================================================
SHEET 3 — Embeddings + rerank (requests/sec per GPU)
All latencies in milliseconds. Throughput is requests/sec/GPU.

GPU | Model | Workload | Concurrency | Batch cap | Quant | Latency p50 | Latency p95 | Throughput | Notes

H100-SXM-80GB | bge-large-en-v1.5 | EMBED-512 | 256 | 256 | FP16 | 14 | 28 | 620 | Ensure tokenizer not in client path.
A100-SXM-80GB | bge-large-en-v1.5 | EMBED-512 | 256 | 256 | FP16 | 19 | 38 | 430 | p95 sensitive to PCIe contention.
L40S-48GB | bge-large-en-v1.5 | EMBED-512 | 256 | 256 | FP16 | 26 | 55 | 290 | Watch for thermal throttling.

H100-SXM-80GB | bge-reranker-large | RERANK-32x128 | 128 | 128 | FP16 | 32 | 66 | 220 | Batch shaping matters; keep harness config fixed.
A100-SXM-80GB | bge-reranker-large | RERANK-32x128 | 128 | 128 | FP16 | 44 | 95 | 150 | Tail can spike if host CPU oversubscribed.

====================================================================
SHEET 4 — Gate guidance (how these baselines are used)
This is the practical interpretation used during patch week.

Perf gate thresholds (default; waivers require Release Eng + SRE approval)
- Generative throughput: regression > -2.0% vs baseline on H100/H200 is FAIL; > -3.0% on A100; > -4.0% on L40S.
- TTFT p95: regression > +3.0% on H100/H200 is FAIL; > +4.0% on A100; > +6.0% on L40S.
- Mixed workload p95 latency: regression > +4.0% on H100/H200 is FAIL unless explained by known variance + rerun.

Rerun rules
- If only a single SKU regresses and the delta is within “expected variance” band: rerun 2 more times; take median.
- If regressions correlate with runner health (clocks/thermals/network): mark run INVALID and reassign runner.

When to require a deeper investigation (even if gates pass)
- MIXED-PROD latency p99 (tracked in perf-canary) increases > +8% but p95 stays flat (often indicates tail pathologies not caught by p95).
- Scheduler regression tests show new queueing/backpressure artifacts (e.g., sawtooth throughput).

====================================================================
Appendix — Runner/environment notes (Q3)
- Runner image update 2025-07-29 changed CUDA minor version; first-run variance increased slightly until autotune cache warmed.
- L40S pool had one chassis with subpar airflow; runs from runner l40s-07 were excluded after 2025-08-05.

Open questions / TODO (before GA)
- Decide whether to add a “prefix-cache-on” scenario for CHAT-8K to better match some Dedicated customer configs (would require separate baseline + clear labeling).
- Consider adding a scheduler micro-benchmark for “bursty arrivals” as a standard scenario (currently only covered by MIXED-PROD).
